newsitem.title: NORWAY: KLM says ex-Norway competition presses cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: KLM says ex-Norway competition presses cargo rates.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV said increased competition on routes to Asia was pressing prices ex-Norway downwards.
Flights from Scandinavian Airlines System and Russia's Aeroflot were squeezing prices, but KLM Cargo business development manager Truls Jakobsen said he hoped prices would rise in the long term.
Jakobsen told Reuters in an interview the Dutch airline was shipping about 400 tonnes on average from Norway per month.
About half of this was salmon and the rest included ship spares, electrical and medical goods.
Salmon, packed with ice in boxes which weighed between 30 to 35 kg each, was hauled in refrigerated trucks to Amsterdam six days a week to meet KLM freighters to the Far East.
Aeroflot was flying regular charters from Norway to Japan.
Although the Russian service offered customers an advantage because it flew shipments from Norway to Japan, it was a different quality of service, Jakobsen said.
"The demand from Tokyo is so big that I think there's room for both of us," Jakobsen said.
Scandinavian Airlines System's Boeing 747 freighter from Gothenburg to Osaka/Macao twice weekly was also adding to competition for salmon shipments.
"They have a premium product that they are selling for lousy prices," Jakobsen said.
KLM flies a Lockheed with a capacity of 15 tonnes including pallets from the southern Swedish city of Malmo to Amsterdam from Tuesday to Saturday.
Jakobsen said the freighter's limited payload capacity and lack of refrigeration facilities made it more logical to truck the salmon to KLM's Amsterdam hub.
"It's actually a better service," Jakobsen said.
"In principle we don't have a capacity limit, but if we do we just hire trucks if we are unable to plan."

Fish markets in Tokyo, Hong Kong, Singapore, Taipei and Seoul were the main destinations for the fresh salmon. Japanese consumers were partial to salmon which weighed three to five kg each while in Taipei fish around seven kg were in demand.
